question.text: Fund ILS holds 2,00,000 shares in SME-listed Company ASME. Current market price INR 25, daily volume 50,000 shares, daily price band -/+2%, opportunity cost 12% p.a. (~0.048% per day, 250 trading days). Assuming sale over 4 consecutive days at successive lower-price-band prices, the total PV of net proceeds comes to INR 48,48,568. What fair value per share should the Fund use for NAV?

explanation.text: The Logic: Fair Value per share = Total PV / Shares = 48,48,568 / 2,00,000 = INR 24.2428. Matches Example 12.11. Illiquid positions cannot be marked at last trade because the fund cannot exit at that price. The Trap: INR 25 is the stale last-trade price (ignores illiquidity discount). INR 23.53 is only the T+3 price. INR 26 is a fabricated premium. Cross-Exam Context: This 'exit-adjusted' valuation is unique to Cat III side-pocket/illiquid methodology. XIX-C tests it; XIX-D (Cat I/II) does not since Cat I/II hold-to-exit anyway. Manager's Pro-Tip: When a position becomes illiquid mid-quarter, trigger side-pocket segregation rather than carry the drag in main NAV - new subscribers otherwise suffer the mark-down while legacy investors benefit from the subsequent recovery. Equalisation won't fix this; side-pocket does.
